title: Intro statistics. Mock Exam A.
instructions: Work independently. You can leave questions unanswered. No score, hints, or solutions appear during this attempt.
personalization: A fictional learning record shows repeated denominator errors in grouped proportions, so Questions 2 and 3 target that skill. Questions 1, 4, and 5 keep coverage of the other confirmed topics.

shared.title: Shared data: support tickets
blocks: The `tickets` data has one row per support ticket. Questions 2 and 3 use this summary table.

table.caption: Fictional counts of tickets by plan and resolution.

questions.title: Read the dataset
prompt: The `tickets` tibble has 40 rows and three columns: `ticket_id`, `plan`, and `wait_min`. Which statements are true?

options.text: Each row represents one support ticket.

option_notes.A: True: the prompt states that each row describes one ticket.
option_notes.B: True: plan names a group membership, not a measured quantity.
option_notes.C: False: 40 is the number of rows (observations); there are three variables.
option_notes.D: True: wait times are measured in minutes.

key.explanation: Rows are observations and columns are variables (packet Section 1).
key.verification: Checked each option against the packet definitions.

questions.title: Name the denominator
questions.personal_target: Repeated reference-group errors in the learning record.
prompt: Using the shared table, what is the proportion of **Plus** tickets that were resolved?

option_notes.A: Uses every ticket as the denominator instead of the Plus group.
option_notes.B: Correct: 18 resolved out of 18 + 6 = 24 Plus tickets.
option_notes.C: Uses all resolved tickets as the denominator, reversing the condition.
option_notes.D: This is the share of all tickets that are Plus, not a resolution rate.

key.explanation: The reference group is the group named after 'of': Plus tickets. Count that group first, then the target cases inside it.

questions.title: Decide whether the method still applies
questions.personal_target: Transfer check: the condition changes, so the student must choose a new reference group.
prompt: Among **resolved** tickets, what proportion came from the Basic plan? Give the fraction and say which group is the denominator.

key.answer: 12 / 30 = 0.4; the denominator is all resolved tickets (12 + 18).
key.explanation: Conditioning on resolved changes the reference group from a plan to the resolved tickets.
key.verification: 12 / 30 = 0.4 computed with Python fractions; equivalent forms 2/5 and 40% accepted.

questions.title: Complete the summary
prompt: Fill in the blank so the pipeline computes the mean wait for each plan while ignoring missing waits.

key.explanation: mean() returns NA when any value is missing unless missing values are removed for that calculation (packet Section 4).
key.verification: Traced from the packet's mean() rule; not executed in R.

questions.title: Count the output rows
prompt: The `tickets` data has 40 rows and 2 plans. How many rows does `tickets |> group_by(plan) |> summarize(n = n())` return?

key.explanation: summarize() returns one row per group, and there are two plans.
key.verification: Follows the packet's one-row-per-group rule; not executed in R.
